# [CS072] Mutable Global State (global-variable)

A package variable is written at run time.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | LOW |
| **Category** | Code Metrics |
| **CWE** | - |
| **OWASP** | - |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

Package variables written after initialization are shared by every goroutine and test, which causes data races and order-dependent behavior. Constants, sentinel errors, compiled regular expressions, lookup tables that are never written and variables guarded by a mutex in the same var block are not reported.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
var currentUser *User

func login(u *User) { currentUser = u }
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
type Session struct{ user *User }

func (s *Session) Login(u *User) { s.user = u }
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [global-variable]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    global-variable: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore global-variable -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** global-variable
```
